Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 22 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana Completes 11 Years of Empowering Small and Micro Entrepreneurs On April 8, 2026, the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY), a transformative initiative of the Government of India (GoI) designed to empower grassroots entrepreneurs across India, completed 11 years. • Since its inception in 2015, the scheme has disbursed over Rs 40.07 lakh crore through 57.79 crore loans, making it one of the world’s largest financial inclusion initiatives. Exam Hints: ✓ What? PMMY completed 11 years ✓ Launched: 8 April 2015 ✓ Loan Categories: o Shishu Loan: up to Rs 50,000; o Kishore Loan: above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh; o Tarun Loan: above Rs 5 lakh and up to Rs 10 lakh; o Tarun Plus Loan: above Rs 10 lakh and up to Rs 20 lakh ✓ Total Loan Disbursement: Rs 40.07 lakh crore through 57.79 crore loans ✓ Women Share: ~2/3rd of loans ✓ New Entrepreneurs: ~1/5th (Rs 12 lakh crore) ✓ Top States: UP, Bihar, Maharashtra. About Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY): Background: PMMY was launched on 8 April 2015 by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi in New Delhi, Delhi, to provide easy, collateral-free micro-credit of up to Rs 10 lakh to non-farm small and micro- entrepreneurs for income-generating activities. Key Pillars: The implementation of financial inclusion programmes in the country is based on three pillars, namely : Banking the Unbanked, Securing the Unsecured and Funding the Unfunded. Implemented by: The scheme is being implemented by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), which works under the Ministry of Finance (MoF). • It is supported by the Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Ltd (MUDRA), a financial institution set up by the GoI under PMMY to support and refinance micro enterprises. • The interest rate is governed by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) guidelines, with flexible repayment terms. Categories: Under the scheme, MUDRA loans have been categorized into four different segments namely, Shishu, Kishore, Tarun, and Tarun Plus, based on loan size: • Shishu: Loans up to Rs 50,000; • Kishore: Loans above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh; • Tarun: Loans above Rs 5 lakh and up to Rs 10 lakh; and • Tarun Plus: Loans above Rs 10 lakh and up to Rs 20 lakh Key Sectors Covered: MUDRA loans cover term financing and working capital requirements across manufacturing, trading and service sectors, including activities allied to agriculture like poultry, dairy, and beekeeping, among others. Loan Disbursement Entities: As per the scheme, Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) such as Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Non-Banking

# Page 23^page=23
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 23 Daily Content PDF Financial Companies (NBFCs), and Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs), among others, disbursed the MUDRA loans. Monitoring Structure: The progress of PMMY is monitored by MUDRA and the DFS, MoF at the national level; and the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) at the state level. • MUDRA has also developed a dedicated web portal, facilitating banks and lending institutions to directly upload their performance and achievement data. Key Accomplishments of PMMY: Women Borrowers: As on March 27 2026, the GoI had disbursed a total of Rs 9.02 lakh crore under the Shishu category, Rs 6.22 lakh crore under Kishore, and Rs 1.09 lakh crore under the Tarun category. • As per the GoI data, two-thirds (approximately 66.66%) of the loans have been sanctioned to women entrepreneurs. • The GoI further revealed that women borrowers accounted for nearly 60% of the total loan accounts, with a total share of 37.45% of the total loan amount disbursed. New Entrepreneurs: Nearly 1/5th (i.e. 12.15 crore loans) of all the loans were extended to first-time entrepreneurs, amounting to Rs 12 lakh crore (30.09% share of the total disbursed amount). • Distribution of MUDRA loans for New Entrepreneurs: 8.80 crore accounts with a sanctioned amount of Rs 2.47 lakh crore and disbursed amount of Rs 2.42 lakh crore (under Shishu category); • 2.79 crore accounts with Rs 5.09 lakh crore sanctioned and Rs 4.87 lakh crore disbursed (Kishor category); • 55 lakh accounts with a sanctioned amount of Rs 4.82 lakh crore and Rs 4.67 lakh crore disbursed (Tarun category). Minority Borrowers: The combined share of minority borrowers including Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), and Other Backward Class (OBC), stood at 45.52% of the loan accounts and 31.77% of the total amount disbursed under PMMY. • For Minority borrowers, the disbursements amounted to Rs 1.33 lakh crore under Shishu, Rs 1.54 lakh crore under Kishor, and Rs 0.62 lakh crore under Tarun. State-wise Distribution: Among all state in the country, Uttar Pradesh (UP) registered the highest loan disbursement under PMMY at Rs 58,111 crore; followed by Bihar (Rs 54,064 crore); and Maharashtra (Rs 50, 762 crore) About Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Ltd (MUDRA): Background: The GoI in the Union Budget for Financial Year 2015–16 (FY16) proposed the setting up of MUDRA Bank to provide refinancing and developmental support to last-mile financiers and strengthen the micro-entrepreneurship ecosystem in India. Formation: Originally, MUDRA was established as a wholly owned subsidiary of Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI). • Later, its capital structure and functions were merged into MUDRA Limited, which continues to work under the SIDBI. Authorised Capital: Rs 1,000 crore Paid-up Capital: Rs 750 crore (fully contributed by SIDBI and the GoI) Chairman – Manoj Mittal

Approval of Two New Airports in Telangana ✓ Ministry: MoCA ✓ Airports Name: Warangal Airport and Adilabad Airport ✓ Key Roles: MoD (Develop airport main infrastructure), MoCA (construct civilian terminal) ✓ Special Feature: Adilabad to serve both civilian use & armed forces training. Adilabad Airport: The MoD will develop the newly approved Adilabad airport, spanning on 370 acres of land, while Airports Authority of India (AAI) will build the civilian terminal. • Adilabad airport will serve a dual purpose, supporting both civilian operations and armed forces training. PFRDA Approves PPFAS AMC to Sponsor Pension Fund under NPS In April 2026, Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), under the Ministry of Finance (MoF), approved PPFAS Asset Management Company (AMC), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Parag Parikh Financial Advisory Services Limited (PPFAS), to act as a sponsor for a pension fund under the National Pension System (NPS). • The initiative aims to manage long-term retirement savings of NPS subscribers with a focus on investor protection, disciplined investing, and consistent returns. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Approval for new pension fund sponsor under NPS ✓ Approved Entity: PPFAS AMC ✓ Regulator: PFRDA ✓ Purpose: Manage long-term retirement savings ✓ Investment Avenues: EQ, G-Secs, Corporate Bonds. Key Details: Structure: A separate pension fund company will be established to manage NPS schemes and invest across Equities (EQ), Government Securities (G-Secs), and Corporate Bonds (CBs), with operations commencing after completion of procedural, regulatory, and infrastructure requirements. NPS Fund Managers: Currently, ten AMCs operate under the NPS, including Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management Co., Axis Asset Management Co., DSP Asset Managers, HDFC Asset Management Co., ICICI Prudential Asset Management Co., Kotak Asset Management Co., LIC Asset Management Co., SBI Funds Management, Tata Asset Management Co., and UTI Asset Management Co. NPS: The NPS, launched in 2004 (for government employees) and extended to all citizens in 2009, is implemented by the PFRDA and allows subscribers to choose and switch fund managers for long-term retirement planning.

Launch of Arogya Van initiative ✓ Launched By: NHAI ✓ Objective: Promote biodiversity & medicinal plants ✓ Phase-I: 67,000+ medicinal trees across 17 land parcels ✓ Coverage: 11 states ✓ Species: ~36 medicinal trees (Neem, Amla, Jamun, etc.) ✓ Sites: Toll plazas, wayside amenities & key highway stretches. About Arogya Van: Phase 1: The first phase covers 17 land parcels over 62.8 hectares, with about 67,462 medicinal trees to be planted across Madhya Pradesh(MP), Haryana, Delhi, Andhra Pradesh(AP), Gujarat, Karnataka, Odisha, Tamil Nadu(TN), Rajasthan, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh. Species: Around 36 types of medicinal trees have been selected, including Neem, Amla, Jamun, Imli (Tamarind), Gular (Cluster Fig), and Maulsari as per suitability to the respective agro-climatic zones. Priority sites: Near toll plazas, wayside amenities, interchanges, cloverleaf junctions, and other prominent highway stretches to maximise visibility and public awareness. Implementation: The initiative will be implemented in accordance with the Government of India’s guidelines on landscaping and tree plantation. INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS India-Egypt Joint Special Forces Exercise ‘Cyclone-IV’ Begins in Egypt On April 9 2026, the fourth edition of the India-Egypt Joint Special Forces Exercise, ‘Cyclone-IV’, officially commenced at Rangers Forces Headquarters, Anshas, Egypt. • The exercise is a 9-day joint engagement, scheduled to be held from April 9 to 17, 2026. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Exercise Cyclone-IV Begins ✓ Between: India–Egypt Joint Special Forces ✓ Where? Anshas, Egypt ✓ Participants: o Indian Army Special Forces (25 personnel) o Egyptian Special Forces ✓ Objective: Enhance interoperability, joint planning & defence cooperation ✓ Focus: Counter-terrorism, special operations & desert warfare ✓ Previous Edition: Cyclone-III (Feb 2025, Rajasthan). Background: Origin: Exercise Cyclone is a bilateral military exercise initiated in 2023, involving joint training between the Indian Army Special Forces and Egyptian Special Forces. Nature: It is an annual exercise conducted alternately in India and Egypt to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation. Previous Edition: The 3rd edition of the India-Egypt Joint Special Forces Exercise CYCLONE-III was held in February 2025, at the Mahajan Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan. Other Exercises: India and Egypt also conduct other joint military engagements, including Exercise Desert Warrior (an Air Force exercise) and Exercise Bright Star. About Exercise Cyclone-IV: Objective: The exercise aims to strengthen joint mission planning capabilities and enhance interoperability by facilitating the exchange of best practices in special operations. Focus: Participating troops will engage in a range of training activities centred on special operational tactics, techniques, and procedures, particularly in desert and semi-desert terrain. Participants: • Indian Contingent: The Indian Army (IA) has deployed a contingent of 25 personnel drawn from its Special Forces units. • Egyptian Contingent: The host nation is represented by personnel from the Egyptian Special Forces Group and Rangers Forces. Joint Operations: • Counter-Terrorism Operations: Neutralising threats in urban and semi-urban environments. • Special Operations: Practising high-stakes tasks like sniper-based operations, tactical combat casualty care, and reconnaissance. • Tactical Drills: Training includes counter-terrorism operations, precision missions, and the exchange of best practices in special warfare. About Egypt: President– Abdel Fattah El-Sisi

Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 27 Daily Content PDF Capital– Cairo Currency– Egyptian Pound (EGP) Tracxn Report: India Ranks 4th Globally in Tech Funding with USD 11.7 Billion in FY26 In April 2026, Tracxn, a leading market intelligence platform, released its ‘India Tech Annual Funding Report 2026’, stating that India’s technology start-ups raised USD 11.7 billion (B) in Financial Year 2025– 26 (FY26), reflecting an 18% decline from USD 14.3 billion in FY25 but a 20% increase over USD 9.7 billion in FY24. • India ranked as the fourth-highest funded country globally in FY26, behind the United States of America (USA) (USD 426B), the United Kingdom (UK) (USD 17.8B), and China (USD 15B), while ahead of Germany (USD 8.4B) and France (USD 8.1B). Exam Hints: ✓ What? India Tech Funding Report 2026 released ✓ Released by: Tracxn ✓ India’s Rank: 4th globally (USD 11.7 billion) ✓ Global Rank: 1st -USA, 2nd-UK, 3rd-China, 5th Germany ✓ Top Sectors: Enterprise Applications, FinTech, Retail ✓ Top Cities: Bengaluru, Mumbai ✓ IPOs: 47 ✓ New Unicorns: 6 ✓ Stages: Early-stage rose to USD 4.8B, while seed and late-stage fell to USD 1.3B and USD 5.6B. Key Findings: Overview: The proprietary report delivers a comprehensive overview of the Indian tech ecosystem in 2025, covering funding trends, sector performance, Initial Public Offerings (IPOs), acquisitions, investor activity, major players, and key industry developments. Stages: Funding trends varied across stages. Seed-stage start-ups raised USD 1.3 billion in FY26, marking a 15% decline from USD 1.5 billion in FY25. • Early-stage funding increased to USD 4.8 billion in FY26, up 33% from USD 3.6 billion in FY25. • Late-stage start-ups raised USD 5.6 billion in FY26, declining 38% from USD 9.2 billion in FY25 but rising 18% from USD 4.7 billion in FY24. Deals: India recorded 13 funding rounds above USD 100 million, with notable deals including Nxtra (USD 710 million), Neysa (USD 600 million), and Inox Clean Energy (USD 344 million). Sectors: Enterprise applications led with USD 3.6 billion, followed by financial technology (FinTech) at USD 2.4 billion (growth observed) and retail at USD 2.4 billion (decline observed). IPOs: A total of 47 IPOs were recorded, marking a 52% increase from FY25, with major listings including Lenskart, Groww, and Meesho. Unicorns: Six unicorns such as Neysa, Raise, Navi, Jumbotail, JSW One MSME, and Juspay, were created in FY26, reflecting a 50% increase compared to FY25 and FY24. Acquisitions: A total of 129 acquisitions were recorded, down 15% from FY25, with top deals including Resulticks acquired by Diginex (USD 2 billion) and Brahma acquired by Polymarket (USD 1.2 billion). Top Cities: Bengaluru (Karnataka) accounted for 33% of total funding, followed by Mumbai(Maharashtra) with a 21% share. Investors: Key investors included Inflection Point Ventures, Rainmatter, and Venture Catalysts (seed-stage), Peak XV Partners, Accel, and Lightspeed Venture Partners (early-stage), and Sofina, Elev8, and Lathe Investment (late-stage).
